A sailboat tacks upwind by zigzagging across the wind, since no vessel can sail
directly into it. The keel resists sideways drift while sails generate lift.

Reefing reduces sail area in strong wind. A prudent skipper reefs the mainsail
early, keeping the boat balanced and the rudder responsive in rising seas.

Navigation by dead reckoning tracks a vessel's position from its known speed,
heading, and elapsed time, corrected for current and leeway.
